packet.title: The host shim (implementation, here)
packet.summary: Moves the JavaScript shim to bindings/host/ as the , with the resolver as a state and a function, leaving the JavaScript export names in bindings/javascript/.

body.p: (): bindings/host/ and target sxml_host, the resolver as a state and a function, three JavaScript export files, tests/host_shim_test.c; sxml.wasm +388 bytes, sxml-full.wasm +561. After . Owns new bindings/host/ (sxml_host.h, sxml_host_internal.h, sxml_host.c, sxml_host_xquery.c, sxml_host_xslt.c, sxml_host_schema.c, sxml_host_full.c, sxml_host_core_features.c, sxml_host_full_features.c, CMakeLists.txt), and the JavaScript shim files it replaces in bindings/javascript/ (they become sxml_javascript_exports.c and sxml_javascript_host.c: the export names and the sxml_host.resolve import), bindings/javascript/CMakeLists.txt, and the top-level CMakeLists.txt line that adds bindings/host.

item.p: Moves the shim as it is, renamed sxml_host_*. It is still written against the public API only ().

The processor configuration gains sxml_host_resolver { void *state; uint32_t (*resolve)(void *state, const sxml_host_resource_request *, sxml_host_resource *); }. Under WASI, the JavaScript export passes a function that calls the import.
The static assertions on 32-bit fields apply under __wasm__ only.
Glossary: now names the export file.
javascript/package, javascript/package_full and javascript/languages_full pass under the wasm preset (WASI SDK and Node are installed here);
sxml.wasm and sxml-full.wasm are within 1 KB of their size before (report both);
a native unit test (tests/host_shim_test.c) runs parse, compile, evaluate and serialize through a resolver function under the debug preset, with 0 leaks.
